- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values if sentiment turns negative or neutral.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or shows strong downward momentum; adjust downward bias in early periods of negative sentiment.
- Lagged price corrections are common: model often overreacts to recent highs and underreacts to lows; apply smoothing or delay correction for 2–3 periods after sharp moves.
- When sentiment shows strong negative spikes (e.g., -0.61 or -0.22 recurring), reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, avoid overshoot correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply downward adjustment for first 5 days if sentiment >0.17.
- Avoid “overshoot after spike” correction: if model peaks after a spike and sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, reduce peak by 5–10% to prevent overcorrection.
